reason: The cited evidence (E1) only states that anti-oxidation coatings are 'still required' for Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys, without providing any data on coating performance, Al2O3 formation, coating-substrate compatibility, or mechanical property retention. The key premises about the coating's protective mechanism, adherence, and non-degradation of mechanical properties are entirely unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Anti-oxidation coatings are required for high-temperature applications of refractory high-entropy alloys in air
An aluminide coating can form a protective Al2O3 scale that acts as an oxygen diffusion barrier
A thin, adherent coating will not degrade the bulk mechanical properties of the substrate
The coating will remain intact and adherent during thermal cycling at ~1000 °C
The baseline mechanical properties of cast HfNbTaTiZr are 8–16% ductility and 163–530 MPa yield strength at 1000 °C
